did_you_know.text: Did you know? Tyre is described as a city situated at the gateway of the sea and as a center of trade connected with many islands and peoples.
Did you know? Tyre’s magnificent construction is described using cypress wood from Senir and cedar from Lebanon, which were used to make the ship’s planks and mast.
Did you know? Tyre’s sail was made of embroidered linen from Egypt, while the blue and purple cloth that covered it came from the islands of Elishah.
Did you know? The people of Tyre are described as having maritime expertise: its skilled men were sailors, and the men of Byblos repaired the ship’s leaks.
Did you know? Chapter 27 presents Tyre as an international trading center, where metals from Tarshish were exchanged for goods.
Did you know? Among the goods brought to Tyre were copper vessels and human beings, as trade was conducted with Greece, Tubal, and Meshech.
Did you know? According to the lament, the east wind was what broke Tyre’s ship in the heart of the sea.
Did you know? When Tyre falls, not only its wealth and merchandise sink into the sea, but also its sailors, shipmasters, merchants, soldiers, and entire population.
Did you know? Mourning for Tyre is described through ancient mourning practices: the seafarers put dust on their heads, roll in ashes, and wear sackcloth.
Did you know? At the end of the chapter, merchants among the nations whistle in astonishment, and Tyre, once a center of wealth, becomes a horror and disappears.
